data.name: Ayyappan
data.gender_notes: Ayyappan is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Ayyappan is a popular Hindu deity, also known as Ayyappan Swamy or Sabarimala Ayyappan. His name means 'Lord of the Sacred Grove'. He is an incarnation of Lord Vishnu, who is believed to protect devotees from all dangers and bestows blessings. The name Ayyappan carries the meaning “Lord of the Sacred Grove” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Ayyappan usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the sacred grove and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Ayyappan belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Sacred Grove.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayyappan total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Ayyappan is a revered figure in the Hindu religious tradition, particularly in the southern Indian states of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. He is known for his martial prowess and stark celibacy. The annual pilgrimage to the Sabarimala Temple is one of the largest religious gatherings in India, attracting millions of devotees every year. The ritualistic traditions and practices associated with the pilgrimage reflect the rich diversity of Hindu culture and the deep devotion of its people.
data.spiritual_significance: Ayyappan is believed to be the dharma raja, or the protector of moral values and the upholder of righteousness. He is also considered a tantrik deity, representing the spiritual path of self-realization and inner purification. Additionally, he is believed to fulfil the desires of his devotees and bestow upon them divine blessings, particularly related to health, wealth, and wisdom. His presence in the hearts and minds of his followers serves as a constant reminder of the importance of leading a virtuous life and seeking the divine within.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Ayyappan is the manifestation of Lord Shiva, embodying strength, compassion, and healing. He is the protector of Sabarimala, a sacred pilgrimage site, inspiring devotion and faith among his followers.

historical_references.reference: Ayyappan is believed to be the incarnation of Lord Vishnu, born to bless the people of Kerala. Ayyappan is also known as Dharma Sastha or Lord of Dharma. The legend says that Ayyappan appeared before a king of Kerala, to protect the people and maintain dharma (moral order).

Ayyappan is also associated with Sabarimala temple, one of the most famous pilgrimage sites in India. The temple is located in the Western Ghats and is believed to be the abode of Ayyappan. The temple has a rich history dating back to the 11th century CE and has been an important center of Hindu pilgrimage since then.

modern_usage.modern_context: In modern times, the Hindu deity Ayyappan is known for his widespread popularity and influence, particularly among the youth. His trends include increased devotion and temple visits, with many young people traveling long distances to Sabarimala in Kerala, one of his most famous temples. Ayyappan's influence extends beyond religious platforms, as he is also commonly seen on social media, where he is the subject of numerous posts, memes, and discussions. Additionally, music platforms like YouTube and Jiosaavn feature numerous songs dedicated to Ayyappan, reflecting his enduring appeal and relevance to contemporary culture.
